instructions: Slice the sujuk into rounds a little under 1/4 inch thick.
Slice the tomatoes. Thinly slice the onion and tear the lettuce into pieces.
In a small bowl, whisk the 2 tbsp olive oil with 1 tbsp lemon juice.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat. It doesn't need oil, because the sujuk gives off its own fat.

Lay the sujuk in the pan in a single layer and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the underside is browned. Flip the rounds and cook the other side for 3 to 4 minutes, until the edges are crisp. Cook in two batches if they don't fit, and move them to a plate.
Warm each pita in the same pan for 20 seconds on each side. Split each one open to make a pocket.
Fill each pita with lettuce, the crisp sujuk, tomato and onion. Drizzle with the lemon dressing.
method_notes: Hadia's Lebanese Cuisine (the only rated page, 5 from 1 vote) stuffs sujuk into a pita pocket; Halal World Depot cooks chopped sujuk until crisp in a pan and dresses the sandwich with oil and lemon, and this one combines the two. Hadia's page uses cheese, which is left out to stay dairy-free. The list promised pickles, but neither source has them, so they are not added. Sujuk is spicy, so buy a mild one if the shop has it.
